summary: Build services without manual Rust setup, start with durable state, and inspect pending deployment approvals. Device login requests dedicated agent credentials; webpage tools distinguish HTML titles from SVG titles.
new: Show pending approval links alongside recorded attempts with crab deploys, including before a service is first deployed
Expose agent login authorizations and pending deployment approvals through the SDK
changed: Request a dedicated agent API key for device login, with its account, permissions and daily budget reviewed in the browser
Include durable remember and recall tools and a 64 MiB storage reservation in crab new scaffolds
fixed: Install missing Rust build tools and the WebAssembly target automatically, making installed tools available to the same build invocation
Check local host status through its health endpoint and explain that crab plans requires a Cloud login
Exclude SVG titles from webpage titles and SEO title counts

summary: Measure service budgets with reproducible Wasm benchmarks, select template versions and control automatic patch updates. The SDK exposes release history, upgrade policies, yanking and template deletion; Markdown and SEO are public services.
new: Measure CPU, rows, peak memory, elapsed time and estimated costs with crab bench, using repeatable JSON Lines cases and arranged HTTP responses
Select an exact template release with crab deploy --from owner/name --version, and opt into stable patch updates with --auto-upgrade
Read retained template releases and manage upgrade policies, release yanking and template deletion through the SDK
changed: Configure web/markdown and web/seo as public running services without publishing templates
Document measured budget sizing, required headroom and destination host ceilings before deployment or publication
fixed: Bound webpage parsing by nodes, nesting, tags and attributes, and size Markdown and SEO tool budgets from WebAssembly workloads
Keep OSV tool CPU budgets within the default 100 ms host ceiling after measuring large responses and maximum-size batches

summary: New agent, web and ops services join Connect integrations. Deploy and publish catalogs by directory, configure service logos, and manage API keys with granular permissions. Schedules and secret destinations now belong to the service image.
new: Share revision-checked, namespaced agent notes with the memory service
Inspect SEO metadata, extract webpage Markdown and collect website analytics with the web services
Monitor endpoints and receive signed, deduplicated events with the uptime and webhooks services
Declare an HTTPS service logo in crab.toml, retained by published templates and private copies
Show purchased and trial credit separately in crab billing, including trial expiry, reserved funds and the hosting recovery deadline
Expose plan credit allowances, eligible account kinds, trial terms and organization creation status through the SDK
Replace an API key's priced-service grants through SDK key updates
Add host invocation scopes for nested and scheduled calls, preserve admission refusal statuses and identify outbound HTTP requests by chain and span
Check on every pull request that changelog.json contains release notes for the current crab-agent version
changed: Organize services under connect, agents, web and ops catalogs, with reusable libraries under services/kits
Scope crab deploy and crab publish to services beneath the supplied directory; -p still selects across the workspace, and publish includes services marked deploy = false
Replace deploy and auto API-key scopes with resource read/write permissions and remove crab key roll; write permission includes read access to the same resource
Embed cron schedules in the image and apply them on every deploy; change crab.toml and redeploy instead of editing schedules on the host or using deploy --pull
Fix credential destinations in the manifest and require fresh provisioning when they change; remove secret host editing and never return saved secret values
Fetch provider OpenAPI specifications into OUT_DIR at build time, with pinned revisions or reviewed digests
Use Cargo default members for routine CI tests and linting, and prepare shared Wasm fixture images with nextest setup scripts
fixed: Reject provisioning undeclared secrets and refuse outbound secret substitution to destinations absent from the manifest
Check the Context.dev OpenAPI source against a reviewed SHA-256 digest

summary: Kits replace guests: auth, crawl, lake, neon, stripe and supabase link into a service's own program. Calls are metered and bounded by CPU time, databases by the size berm.toml gives them, and crab installs and upgrades itself from GitHub releases.
new: Link a kit into a service by depending on it: a kit declares its secrets, hosts and migrations in a berm.toml of its own, the build finds each kit among the crates compiled into the image, and what the kit declares joins the service's manifest and its tables live in the service's database
Link kits through crabkit, a feature per kit: crabkit = { features = ["stripe"] }, called as crabkit::stripe
Build a service's image with crab build [dir], which prints the path of the finished image under target/berm; crab deploy builds it the same way
Use the auth kit for accounts and sessions, stripe for checkout and subscriptions, supabase for PostgREST and Storage, and neon for Postgres over HTTP
Crawl the sites a service watches with the crawl kit: robots.txt and sitemaps, pages of the kinds it names, the URLs it lists and the links its crawler finds, recrawled when they change
Follow feeds and records with the lake kit: RSS 2.0, RSS 1.0 and Atom, threads under items, and a version stored per change of a record
Install crab with curl -fsSL https://crab.talk/install.sh | sh, and upgrade it in place with crab upgrade, each checked against GitHub's digest of the release asset
Start a service's database on Cloud from the seed berm.toml names, on its first deploy
Bound a service's database with [database] size in berm.toml, from 64KiB to 10GiB, 1GiB when unset
Subscribe from a trial at once with crab billing plan
Fetch many URLs in one call with berm_lang::http::fetch_all, each with its own timeout and the body bytes it takes
Declare fetch hosts as *.domain or *, a host reached only by a pattern refused at an address that is not public
Read random bytes with berm.random, and name the end user the rest of a call's chain runs for with berm.vouch
Run bermd with a development dashboard behind its dashboard feature, from ghcr.io/crabtalk/crab/berm or the repository's compose file
Build a product's services on crab with the crab skill in skills/crab
changed: Meter and bound each call by CPU time in microseconds in place of wasm instructions: budgets take cpu, and bermd takes --max-cpu-millis
Have crab new take berm-lang from crab's git tag of the CLI's release

Write a service's tools as functions marked #[berm_lang::tool(...)] anywhere in its crate, taking public, anonymous, query, cron, stripe and callers(...), in place of #[berm_lang::program] on a module and its #[public], #[cron] and other attributes
Declare a service's syscalls, secrets, programs, database, readme and buffer in berm.toml in place of #[berm_lang::program(...)]
Build a service as a cdylib library, [lib] crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"], with no bin target and no bin/main.rs
Refuse an image without the .berm.program section crab build appends, which a bare cargo build leaves out
Name a feed's Kind (chronological, unordered or records) in lake in place of its chronological flag, and give a listed item's posted as an Option, None when the feed gives no date
Collapse the crawl kit's migrations into one
Cut a response at the body bytes its request names in bermd, where it failed past 16MiB
Take Duration fields of berm_host::Config as "50ms" or "60s"
Move auth and stripe's services into fixtures, the kits staying libraries
Move berm_lang::html into the crab-html crate, which reads a page's title, meta, links and text
Drop the plan's storage rate, a plan's stored bytes the cap its services reserve against

Name the kit crates crabkit-auth, crabkit-crawl, crabkit-lake, crabkit-neon, crabkit-stripe and crabkit-supabase. A kit's migrations are recorded under its crate's name, so a database that ran them as crab-* runs them again and must be recreated
fixed: Read a fetch's host as the URL reaches it, so a URL spelled to look like another host, or an address written as a number, is held to the manifest and to bermd's public-address check
Bound every read of guest memory, so berm.random and berm.vouch cannot make the host allocate past it
Refuse a Supabase Storage path with an empty, . or .. segment, which reached another bucket
Hold the URLs a program lists to the site's robots.txt, match its * patterns in linear time, read it past a byte order mark, and compare its patterns percent-encoded
Keep a site's URLs when every sitemap fails, and split a round's shared sitemap budget so it cannot be overrun
Store an undated item and one posted at the watermark in a chronological feed, read nested RSS elements' text apart, and refuse out-of-range dates
End HTML tags at their real end and match tag names whole in crab-html, and keep an unknown entity as written
Refuse a database size under 64KiB, which left a database unlimited, and put the old size back when a deploy is refused
Show CPU in the dashboard, which broke on the renamed meter
Copy a deploy's seed through a temporary directory removed on every exit
